transcript: Last night, I saw The Welkin at Atlantic Theater Company, a gripping dramedy by Lucy Kirkwood about democracy, motherhood, prejudice, and assumptions. Set in England in the 1700s, 12 women are gathered as a jury to decide the fate of another woman who's trying to avoid the death penalty by claiming that she's pregnant. Despite the time period, this piece feels very timely in what it shows of how we make assumptions about one another, how our ideological opinions influence and sometimes cloud our own judgment, and really how depraved we can be in desperate situations. The performances are really captivating, and although this is largely a display of ensemble work, I also wanted to call out Haley Wong and Sandra Oh who are featured pretty heavily and who are both really amazing in this. The writing I found quite sharp and funny, but as the plot progresses, things really turn and by the end there isn't a lot to laugh about which feels intentional. What I love the most about this play is how big it is — big cast, big laughs, big twists and turns, bold directorial choices. I feel like I haven't seen such a big sprawling ensemble play like this since maybe The Ferryman on Broadway in 2018. I would love for The Welkin to move uptown as well, but for now it's still in downtown previews and I do think that there's some work left to be done on it. That said I really appreciate the bold swings it's already taking and the writing, acting, and direction are already in very good shape. Needless to say, I would recommend this. With that, another program for my collection.
